T raditional rulers and other dignitaries on Saturday gathered at St Peter’s Church, Faji, Lagos Island, as Oyindamola Abimbola and Olusegun Olaleke exchanged marital vows. The wedding attracted family members, friends and other distinguished guests, who turned up in beautiful native attires to celebrate the couple. The church was also beautifully decorated for the occasion, giving the venue a colourful and lovely look. The traditional rulers were among the guests who stood out at the ceremony, as they appeared in flowing agbadas, complemented by traditional beads and staffs. Their presence added a touch of royalty to the celebration, while the bishops and other clerics also gave the occasion a special significance. The bride, Oyindamola, is the daughter of Mr Oluyomi and Mrs Modupeola Amoye, while the groom, Olusegun, is the son of Aare (Dr) Olukayode Awosanya and Yeye Aare (Mrs) Abimbola Awosanya. Add us to your Preferred Sources Among the officiating ministers were the Diocesan Bishop of Lagos, the Rt Revd Ifedola Okupevi, and the Archdeacon of Lagos, the Ven Tunde Oduwole. The solemnisation of the marriage began with the bride walking into the church alongside her father, who accompanied her as she made her way to meet her groom. The couple later exchanged marital vows, promising to remain committed to each other. A hymn followed the exchange of vows as the service continued. One of the significant moments of the ceremony was the blessing of the wedding rings by the bishops. After the blessing, Abimbola and Olaleke exchanged rings, sealing their promises to one another before the congregation. The bishops subsequently pronounced them husband and wife, followed by prayers and blessings for their marriage. The parents of both the bride and groom also gave their consent to the union and blessed the couple as they began their journey together. The service also featured the administration of Holy Communion, with gifts prepared for the Eucharistic Prayer. The couple later signed the wedding register, while their marriage certificate was presented during the proceedings. The newlyweds were also formally introduced to the congregation, marking another memorable moment in the ceremony.
